label: Access Key
depicts: Small round headed key with two short teeth on a straight shaft
use_when: Use when the interface wants the simplest upright key silhouette with a round head.
avoid_when: Do not use for the angled or paired key icons when the straight vertical key is intended.

label: Access Key
depicts: Standard key with a round head hole an angled shoulder and two bottom teeth
use_when: Use when the interface wants a more classic side view key with a round head opening.
avoid_when: Do not use for the upright or paired keys when the angled body should remain visible.

label: Access Key
depicts: Two keys hanging together with round heads and overlapping shafts
use_when: Use when the interface wants to show multiple keys grouped together rather than one single key.
avoid_when: Do not use for lone keys when the icon clearly shows two overlapping key shapes.

label: Access Key
depicts: Two outline keys side by side with mirrored shafts and round heads
use_when: Use when the interface wants a balanced double key symbol rather than overlapping loose keys.
avoid_when: Do not use for the hanging key pair when the two keys should read as parallel outlines.

label: Edit
depicts: Document outline with two short text lines and a small pencil badge
use_when: Use when the interface wants editing attached to a document or file rather than a free pencil.
avoid_when: Do not use for the standalone edit icons when the file outline is the key visible cue.
